headline: Meta plans to open-source Muse Spark 1.2, one of its strongest AI models, and its shares rose before the market opened.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a major company move with a share reaction, stated by the CEO in an essay and reported by IBTimes.
importance_line: Developers would get a powerful model to build on and US policymakers face a call to ease training-data rules, but the honest doubt is that these are Meta's own arguments in an essay, and its shares were still down about 10 percent this year.
summary: International Business Times reports that Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said in an essay that Meta will release Muse Spark 1.2, one of its strongest AI models, as open source, meaning outside developers can use it, along with several models called Muse Glimmer. He also urged Washington to ease training-data restrictions that he says leave American labs at a disadvantage, and Meta's shares rose almost 2 percent before trading, although they are down about 10 percent this year.
notes: Read in full from IBTimes (2,323 chars). Essay quotes are Zuckerberg's. Left out for length: Sen. Bernie Sanders's call for an AI pause, which the article also reports.
